activities.title: Watch lucha libre from the cheap seats
activities.description: Masked wrestling in Mexico City's Arena México, taken seriously and not seriously at the same time. The crowd is the show.

snapshot.visa: Visa-free up to 180 days (US), 6 months (UK)

countries.name: Costa Rica
countries.blurb: A small country wedged between two oceans, with more of its land protected than almost anywhere else on earth — cloud forest, rainforest, volcanoes and coastline all within a few hours' drive of each other.
countries.uniqueness: Costa Rica abolished its army in 1948 and put the savings into parks, schools and health care instead — a quarter of the country is now protected land. It sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire, so active volcanoes are a normal part of the scenery, and the two coasts are different enough in feel and weather that picking one over the other changes the whole trip.

seasons.label: Dry season
seasons.note: Verano — sunny skies, calm Pacific seas and the busiest, priciest window. Book Easter week (April 5–12, 2026) well ahead.

seasons.label: Green season
seasons.note: Invierno — afternoon showers, lush landscapes, thinner crowds and lower prices. Mornings are usually still clear.

seasons.label: Caribbean dry spell
seasons.note: The Caribbean coast doesn't follow the same pattern as the Pacific side — this is its driest, sunniest stretch.

seasons.label: Peak green season
seasons.note: Heaviest rain on the Pacific side, but also the emptiest beaches and the best hotel rates of the year.

activities.title: Zipline through cloud forest canopy
activities.description: Monteverde popularized the zipline circuit and still runs some of the longest lines, gliding over a forest that's usually wrapped in mist.

activities.title: Walk a hanging bridge trail
activities.description: Suspension bridges strung through the canopy at Monteverde or Arenal put you at eye level with the treetops instead of looking up from the forest floor.

activities.title: Soak in hot springs below a volcano
activities.description: Arenal's eruptions stopped in 2010, but the geothermal water it left behind still feeds pools ranging from resort-fancy to a free river soak.

activities.title: Watch scarlet macaws in Carara
activities.description: One of the most reliable spots in the country to see the birds in the wild, flying in pairs at dawn and dusk between the park and the coast.

activities.title: Spot sloths at your own pace
activities.description: They're everywhere once you know how to look — Manuel Antonio and Cahuita both have guides skilled at spotting them, but a slow walk anywhere in the canopy usually works.

activities.title: Surf the Pacific coast
activities.description: Tamarindo and Santa Teresa are the well-known breaks with schools for beginners; Pavones has one of the longest lefts in the world for the experienced.

activities.title: Watch turtles nest at Tortuguero
activities.description: Leatherbacks, greens and hawksbills come ashore on the Caribbean coast, reachable only by boat or small plane through a maze of canals.

activities.title: Raft the Pacuare River
activities.description: Class III–IV whitewater through a jungle gorge, often run as a multi-day trip with riverside camps rather than a single-day rush.

activities.title: Hike Corcovado National Park
activities.description: National Geographic once called it the most biologically intense place on earth — tapirs, all four Costa Rican monkey species and jaguar tracks, reachable only with a licensed guide.

activities.title: Snorkel or dive Isla del Caño
activities.description: A protected biological reserve off the Osa Peninsula with visibility and marine life well beyond what the mainland coast offers.

activities.title: Stand at the edge of an active crater
activities.description: Poás and Irazú both have drivable access to viewpoints over steaming, sulfur-yellow craters — Poás can close on short notice depending on activity.
activities.when: Morning visits, before clouds roll in

activities.title: Ride a horse through Guanacaste ranchland
activities.description: The country's cowboy heartland, dry and dusty compared to the rest of Costa Rica, with working cattle ranches that take guests out on horseback.

activities.title: Watch the sunset from Manuel Antonio's beaches
activities.description: A small park with an outsized reputation, packing rainforest, monkeys and a handful of postcard beaches into a couple of square miles.

activities.title: Try a soda for lunch
activities.description: Family-run diners serving casado — rice, beans, plantain, salad and a choice of meat or fish — are the honest, everyday version of Costa Rican food.

activities.title: Drink coffee where it's grown
activities.description: The Central Valley's volcanic soil produces some of the country's best beans — tours around Naranjo and Tarrazú walk the process from cherry to cup.

activities.title: Kayak through mangroves
activities.description: Damas Island near Manuel Antonio and the canals around the Nicoya Peninsula are quiet enough to paddle past herons, caimans and monkeys without a motor.

activities.title: Go night walking in the rainforest
activities.description: A different set of animals comes out after dark — red-eyed frogs, tarantulas, kinkajous — best done with a guide's spotlight and local knowledge.

activities.title: Spend a slow day at an eco-lodge
activities.description: Much of the appeal here isn't a single activity but the pace — a hammock, birdsong, and no schedule, which is the point for a lot of visitors.

activities.title: Cross to the Caribbean side
activities.description: Puerto Viejo and Cahuita move at reggae-inflected, Afro-Caribbean rhythm that feels like a different country from the Pacific beach towns.

activities.title: Whitewater raft the Sarapiquí
activities.description: A gentler, more accessible run than the Pacuare, close enough to San José for a day trip and still genuinely fun.

activities.title: Watch the Arenal volcano from a distance
activities.description: On a clear night the cone is lit by the moon and, occasionally, still glows — even dormant it dominates the skyline around La Fortuna.

snapshot.visa: Visa-free for most US/UK/EU travelers, typically up to 90 days
snapshot.currency: Costa Rican colón (CRC) — USD widely accepted

countries.name: Norway
countries.blurb: A coastline cut so deep by ice that it takes weeks to sail its length — fjords, midnight sun, polar night, and small wooden towns holding on to steep, narrow ground.
countries.uniqueness: Norway's coastline, fjords included, is long enough to circle the earth roughly one and a half times, and almost none of it is straight. Daylight is the country's real variable — near-endless sun in June, four or five hours of it in December — and what's worth doing changes completely depending on which one you get.

seasons.label: Midnight sun
seasons.note: Long light, open mountain roads, sunny fjord cruises and the warmest hiking weather. Also the busiest and priciest months.

seasons.label: Shoulder season
seasons.note: May brings waterfalls at full snowmelt power and green valleys before the crowds; September starts to bring the dark back for aurora hunting.

seasons.label: Northern lights window
seasons.note: Needs real darkness, so this only works once the midnight sun ends. Tromsø, Alta and the Lofoten Islands are the reliable bases.

seasons.label: Deep winter
seasons.note: Snowshoeing, dog sledding, whale watching off the north coast and the best statistical odds for aurora, alongside short days and closed mountain passes.

activities.title: Cruise or drive the Geirangerfjord
activities.description: A UNESCO-listed fjord with waterfalls dropping straight into the water and farms clinging to ledges that look impossible to reach.

activities.title: Ride the Flåm Railway
activities.description: One of the steepest standard-gauge railways in the world, twenty minutes down a mountainside past waterfalls, connecting to Sognefjord below.

activities.title: Hike to Preikestolen
activities.description: A flat rock plateau 604 metres above Lysefjord — a demanding but non-technical hike that ends at one of the most photographed views in the country.

activities.title: Hike Trolltunga
activities.description: A longer, tougher day than Preikestolen — a rock ledge jutting horizontally over a lake, ten to twelve hours round trip.

activities.title: Chase the northern lights
activities.description: Clear, dark skies away from town lights are the only requirement besides luck — Tromsø and the Lofoten Islands give the best odds of both.

activities.title: Stay up for the midnight sun
activities.description: North of the Arctic Circle the sun simply doesn't set for weeks — a hike or a fjord kayak at what should be midnight is a genuinely disorienting pleasure.

activities.title: Explore the Lofoten Islands
activities.description: Jagged granite peaks rising straight from the sea, red fishing cabins called rorbuer, and white-sand beaches that look tropical until you touch the water.
activities.when: Jun–Aug for hiking, Sep–Mar for aurora

activities.title: Watch orcas and humpbacks off Tromsø
activities.description: Herring overwinter in the fjords north of Tromsø, and whales follow them in — boat trips run from the town most winter mornings.

activities.title: Walk the wooden streets of Bergen
activities.description: Bryggen's tilted, colourful timber buildings along the harbour are what's left of a Hanseatic trading post, now a UNESCO site and the gateway to the fjords.

activities.title: Spend a day in Oslo
activities.description: A compact capital mixing Viking ship museums, a fjord-side opera house you can walk on the roof of, and forest right at the edge of the city limits.

activities.title: Go dog sledding
activities.description: Run by mushers across Finnmark and around Tromsø, usually paired with a night in a lavvo tent or cabin under whatever the sky is doing.

activities.title: Visit a Sámi reindeer herd
activities.description: The indigenous Sámi have herded reindeer across the Arctic north for centuries — some family operations now host visitors for a meal and a look at the herd.

activities.title: Ride the Norway in a Nutshell route
activities.description: A single-day chain of train, fjord ferry and mountain bus connecting Bergen and Oslo through Flåm and the Aurlandsfjord.

activities.title: Eat at a harbourside fish market
activities.description: Bergen's Fisketorget and Oslo's harbour stalls sell what came in that morning — king crab, cod, prawns eaten standing up.

activities.title: Kayak a fjord at your own pace
activities.description: Rentals are available on most of the accessible fjords — Nærøyfjord and Geirangerfjord both have calm enough water for a half-day paddle.

activities.title: Take the Hurtigruten coastal ferry
activities.description: A working mail-and-passenger route running the length of the coast from Bergen to Kirkenes, stopping in dozens of small ports along the way.

activities.title: Visit the Arctic Cathedral in Tromsø
activities.description: A glass-and-concrete triangle on the edge of the fjord, striking by day and lit from within after dark.

activities.title: Ski or snowboard in the fjords
activities.description: Norway's downhill scene doesn't get the attention of the Alps, but resorts like Hemsedal and Trysil, and heli-skiing around the Lyngen Alps, deliver serious terrain.

activities.title: Sample brunost and open sandwiches
activities.description: A caramel-brown goat cheese that divides visitors, usually served on flatbread or crispbread alongside cured fish and cold cuts for a typical breakfast.

activities.title: Stand at the North Cape
activities.description: A cliff plateau marketed as continental Europe's northernmost point, with the midnight sun visible from mid-May to the end of July.

snapshot.visa: Visa-free 90 days (Schengen) for US/UK/EU

countries.name: Kenya
countries.blurb: Savanna running to the horizon, the Great Migration crossing it twice a year, and a coastline of white sand and old Swahili trading towns that most safari itineraries skip entirely.
countries.uniqueness: Kenya sits directly on the equator, which keeps its seasons driven by rainfall rather than temperature — the same warm weather runs most of the year, and it's the wet or dry months, not hot or cold ones, that decide where the animals and the crowds are. The Maasai Mara is the northern half of the same ecosystem as Tanzania's Serengeti, so the migration simply walks back and forth across an invisible border.

seasons.label: Long dry season
seasons.note: The classic safari window — wildlife concentrated around water, and from July the wildebeest herds arrive in the Mara with dramatic river crossings through September.

seasons.label: Short dry season
seasons.note: Mild, mostly dry, with newborn wildlife on the plains and generally easier photography light than the peak months.

seasons.label: Long rains
seasons.note: The heaviest rain of the year — some camps close, roads get difficult, but rates drop sharply and the landscape turns green.

seasons.label: Short rains
seasons.note: Brief afternoon showers rather than all-day rain, lower prices than peak season, and a quieter, greener Mara.

activities.title: Watch the Mara river crossings
activities.description: Wildebeest and zebra crossing crocodile-filled water is the single most photographed moment of the migration — never guaranteed on a given day, but reliable across the season.

activities.title: Go on a dawn game drive in the Maasai Mara
activities.description: Lion, leopard, cheetah, elephant and buffalo all present year-round, with the light and animal activity both at their best in the first hours after sunrise.

activities.title: Take a hot air balloon safari
activities.description: A sunrise float over the Mara plains, finishing with a champagne breakfast set up in the bush below — one of the more expensive mornings you can spend in Kenya, and one people rarely regret.

activities.title: Track rhino in Lake Nakuru or Ol Pejeta
activities.description: Both black and white rhino are protected in fenced or heavily patrolled conservancies, a rare chance to see a species that's disappeared from most of its former range.

activities.title: Meet the last northern white rhinos
activities.description: Ol Pejeta Conservancy is home to the two remaining northern white rhinos on earth, both female, kept under guard as science looks for ways to save the subspecies.

activities.title: Visit a Maasai village
activities.description: Community visits arranged through the village itself, not a drive-by, offer a look at a culture still built around cattle, age-set traditions and a pastoralist life that persists alongside the safari industry.

activities.title: Spend a day at Lamu Old Town
activities.description: A UNESCO World Heritage Swahili town on an island off the north coast — no cars, carved wooden doors, dhows in the harbour, and thirteenth-century trading roots.

activities.title: Snorkel or dive Watamu Marine Park
activities.description: Coral gardens, turtles and reef fish just off a coastline most safari visitors never reach, with a slower, beach-town pace than the parks inland.

activities.title: Climb Mount Kenya
activities.description: Africa's second-highest peak, with routes that don't require technical climbing to reach Point Lenana, moving through five distinct climate zones on the way up.

activities.title: See flamingos on the Rift Valley lakes
activities.description: Lake Nakuru and Lake Bogoria draw huge flocks depending on algae levels, which shift year to year — sometimes a thin pink line on the water, sometimes a solid one.

activities.title: Walk with a Samburu guide in the north
activities.description: Samburu National Reserve holds species not found further south — Grevy's zebra, reticulated giraffe, gerenuk — in a drier, more remote landscape than the Mara.

activities.title: Track chimpanzees at Ol Pejeta's sanctuary
activities.description: The only place in Kenya to see chimpanzees, a sanctuary for animals rescued from the pet and bushmeat trade elsewhere in Africa, not a native population.

activities.title: Eat nyama choma
activities.description: Grilled meat, usually goat, cooked over an open fire and shared straight off the board — the default centrepiece of a Kenyan weekend meal.

activities.title: Spend a morning in a Nairobi market
activities.description: The Maasai Market rotates locations through the week, selling beadwork, carvings and fabric direct from makers — good for bargaining and better for conversation.

activities.title: Visit the Giraffe Centre in Nairobi
activities.description: A conservation centre for the endangered Rothschild's giraffe, with a raised platform that puts visitors at head height with the animals.

activities.title: Feed an orphaned elephant
activities.description: The David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust in Nairobi hand-raises orphaned elephant calves for eventual release back into Tsavo — public visiting hours are brief and popular.

activities.title: Go on safari in Amboseli, under Kilimanjaro
activities.description: Kenya's answer to postcard Africa — elephant herds crossing open plains with Kilimanjaro's snowcap behind them, clearest at dawn before clouds build.

activities.title: Kitesurf or relax on Diani Beach
activities.description: White sand and warm water on the south coast, with a well-established kitesurfing scene alongside straightforward beach time.

activities.title: Take a walking safari
activities.description: A handful of conservancies allow armed-guide walking safaris — slower, quieter, and focused on tracks, dung and smaller life the vehicles drive past.

activities.title: Watch the sunset over the Mara plains
activities.description: No specific site — just find a high point in camp or on a drive as the light goes gold, which is when a lot of the wildlife starts moving again.

snapshot.visa: eTA required online before boarding — no visa on arrival, about $30

faq.q: Is Kenya safe for tourists?
faq.a: Established safari circuits — the Maasai Mara, Amboseli, Lake Nakuru, and the main coastal resorts — see heavy tourism and are generally safe with a reputable operator. As with any destination, check current travel advisories for specific regions before you go, particularly near the Somali border.

faq.q: How much does a Kenya safari cost?
faq.a: Budget camping safaris start around $150-200 per person per day; mid-range lodge safaris run $300-500; luxury tented camps can exceed $1,000 per day. Park fees, which fund conservation, are a fixed cost layered on top regardless of comfort level.

faq.q: When is the best time for the wildebeest migration?
faq.a: July through October, with the dramatic river crossings into the Maasai Mara concentrated in August and September. The migration is a year-round cycle across the Serengeti-Mara ecosystem, but this window is when the herds are in Kenya specifically.

faq.q: Do I need a visa or eTA for Kenya?
faq.a: Yes — Kenya requires an Electronic Travel Authorization (eTA) for nearly all visitors, applied for online before you fly. There is no visa on arrival anymore, so this has to be sorted before you board, not after you land.

faq.q: How many days do you need for a Kenya safari?
faq.a: A focused Maasai Mara safari works in 3-4 days. A week to ten days lets you combine the Mara with Amboseli or Lake Nakuru and add a few days on the coast at Diani Beach afterward.

faq.q: Is Kenya expensive?
faq.a: It sits in the middle — safari park fees and lodges push costs up, but Nairobi and the coast are affordable by comparison, and budget camping safaris make the classic experience accessible without a luxury-trip price tag.

countries.name: New Zealand
countries.blurb: Two main islands split by climate and character — the North warmer and more populated, the South colder, wilder and stacked with the mountains, fjords and glaciers most people picture when they imagine the country.
countries.uniqueness: New Zealand was one of the last large landmasses on earth to be settled by people, arriving with Polynesian voyagers roughly seven hundred years ago, which is part of why its wildlife evolved so strangely — flightless birds with no mammal predators to avoid until humans and their animals showed up. Being in the Southern Hemisphere flips its seasons opposite the northern half of the world, which trips up more travellers than any packing list warns them about.

seasons.label: Summer
seasons.note: Long, warm days and the busiest season, especially over the New Zealand school holidays around late December and January. Best for beaches and the Great Walks.

seasons.label: Autumn
seasons.note: Stable weather, fewer crowds and colour changes in the South Island's beech forests — many consider this the best all-round window for hiking and driving.

seasons.label: Winter
seasons.note: Ski season around Queenstown, Wānaka and the central North Island, with snow closing some high mountain passes elsewhere.

seasons.label: Spring
seasons.note: Wildflowers and newborn lambs across the country, but also the wettest season in many regions — pack for both sun and rain.

activities.title: Hike a Great Walk
activities.description: Nine officially maintained multi-day tracks, from the Milford Track's fjords to the Tongariro Northern Circuit's volcanic craters — huts need booking well ahead in summer.
activities.when: Oct–Apr for most, check individual track conditions

activities.title: Cruise Milford Sound
activities.description: A fjord, despite the name, with waterfalls dropping hundreds of metres straight into the water and rain that only makes it more dramatic.

activities.title: Bungee jump where it began
activities.description: AJ Hackett's Kawarau Bridge near Queenstown was the world's first commercial bungee site — still running the original jump alongside newer, higher ones nearby.

activities.title: Walk on a glacier in South Westland
activities.description: Fox and Franz Josef glaciers descend unusually close to sea level through rainforest — access changes yearly as the ice retreats, so guided helicopter trips are now standard.

activities.title: Go stargazing in a Dark Sky Reserve
activities.description: Aoraki Mackenzie is one of the largest dark sky reserves on earth — the Milky Way is visible without a telescope on a clear night.

activities.title: Soak in Rotorua's geothermal pools
activities.description: A town that smells faintly of sulfur from the geysers and mud pools underneath it, with both commercial spas and free public hot pools.

activities.title: Learn about Māori culture at a marae
activities.description: Cultural centres in Rotorua and elsewhere host guided visits with a hāngī feast cooked in an earth oven and a haka performance explained in context.

activities.title: Drive the Milford Road
activities.description: One of the world's great scenic drives, from Te Anau to Milford Sound through the Hollyford and Eglinton valleys, past the Homer Tunnel.

activities.title: Skydive over Lake Taupō or Queenstown
activities.description: Two of the most scenic drop zones on earth — one over a volcanic lake, the other over the Remarkables mountain range and Lake Wakatipu.

activities.title: Spot kiwi on a night walk
activities.description: The national bird is nocturnal and shy — Stewart Island and a handful of guided sanctuaries offer the best realistic odds of seeing one wild.

activities.title: Sail or kayak the Bay of Islands
activities.description: A cluster of 144 islands off the North Island's east coast, warm enough for swimming and dolphin sightings in summer.

activities.title: Explore Hobbiton
activities.description: The actual film set from The Lord of the Rings and The Hobbit, kept standing as a permanent, walkable attraction on a working Waikato farm.

activities.title: Wine taste in Marlborough or Central Otago
activities.description: Marlborough built its name on sauvignon blanc; Central Otago, one of the world's southernmost wine regions, does the same for pinot noir.

activities.title: Whale watch from Kaikōura
activities.description: A deep ocean trench close to shore brings sperm whales year-round, with humpbacks and orca passing through at certain times of year.

activities.title: Ski or snowboard the Southern Alps
activities.description: Queenstown and Wānaka anchor the country's main ski fields, with terrain ranging from beginner slopes to genuine backcountry.

activities.title: Walk the Tongariro Alpine Crossing
activities.description: A one-day, nineteen-kilometre trail across active volcanic terrain — emerald lakes, a crater rim and, on a clear day, views to Mount Taranaki.

activities.title: Eat fish and chips by a harbour
activities.description: An unofficial national dish, best eaten straight from the paper on a wharf — nearly every coastal town has a shop worth stopping for.

activities.title: Jet boat a canyon river
activities.description: Shallow-draft boats built for New Zealand's braided rivers, spinning through canyons at speed — Shotover River near Queenstown is the best known.

activities.title: Spend a day in Wellington
activities.description: A small, hilly capital known for its coffee culture, film industry ties through Weta Workshop, and a waterfront that fills up on any sunny afternoon.

activities.title: Visit a colony of yellow-eyed penguins
activities.description: Among the rarest penguin species on earth, breeding on the Otago Peninsula and Catlins coast — viewing hides keep a respectful distance for the birds.

snapshot.visa: NZeTA required before boarding (visa waiver)

countries.name: Croatia
countries.blurb: A thousand islands scattered down the Adriatic, walled medieval towns still lived in rather than preserved behind glass, and lakes so clear and blue-green they look edited.
countries.uniqueness: Croatia's coastline includes more than a thousand islands, though only about fifty are inhabited, which is why island-hopping by ferry is less a tourist activity here than the ordinary way locals get around. The country only became independent in 1991, and its old Venetian, Austro-Hungarian and Yugoslav layers are still visible stacked on top of each other in the architecture, if you know where to look.

seasons.label: Spring
seasons.note: Plitvice's waterfalls run at full snowmelt power, and the coast warms up without the July–August crowds or prices.

seasons.label: Early summer
seasons.note: The Adriatic starts to feel like a proper summer sea while towns like Dubrovnik and Split are still manageable before peak season hits.

seasons.label: Peak summer
seasons.note: The warmest water and the fullest islands — cruise ship crowds in Dubrovnik are at their heaviest, and prices follow.

seasons.label: Autumn
seasons.note: Warm water, thinning crowds, wine harvest in Istria and Dalmatia, and Plitvice's forests turning colour — often called the best all-round window.

activities.title: Walk the walls of Dubrovnik's Old Town
activities.description: Nearly two kilometres of intact medieval fortification circling the city, with Adriatic views on one side and terracotta rooftops on the other.

activities.title: Explore Diocletian's Palace in Split
activities.description: A Roman emperor's retirement palace from 305 AD that never stopped being lived in — it's now the core of the old city, with shops and homes built into the ancient walls.

activities.title: Walk the boardwalks at Plitvice Lakes
activities.description: Sixteen terraced lakes connected by waterfalls, with wooden walkways crossing directly over the turquoise water — the country's most-visited natural site.
activities.when: Apr–May, Sep–Oct for water flow and crowds

activities.title: Swim in the Adriatic off Hvar or Vis
activities.description: Some of the clearest water in the Mediterranean, with Vis in particular kept quieter by its distance from the mainland and years as a former military base.

activities.title: Ferry-hop the Dalmatian islands
activities.description: Split acts as the main hub, with regular connections to Hvar, Brač, Vis and Korčula — island rhythm slows down fast once you're off the mainland.

activities.title: Visit the Blue Cave on Biševo
activities.description: Sunlight refracting through an underwater opening turns the cave's interior water a glowing electric blue for a few hours around midday.

activities.title: Kayak the Elaphiti Islands near Dubrovnik
activities.description: A quieter half-day paddle through a small archipelago just offshore, well away from the Old Town's crowds.

activities.title: Explore Krka National Park
activities.description: Waterfalls similar to Plitvice's but with a swimming area at the base of Skradinski Buk — one of the few Croatian falls you're allowed into the water at.

activities.title: Wander Rovinj's old town in Istria
activities.description: A former fishing village on a former island, its pastel houses climbing a hill to a bell tower modeled on Venice's — Istria's answer to the Dalmatian coast, with an Italian accent.

activities.title: Truffle hunt in Istria
activities.description: The Motovun forest produces both white and black truffles, and several family operations run guided hunts with trained dogs followed by a truffle lunch.

activities.title: Taste wine on the Pelješac Peninsula
activities.description: Home to Croatia's best-known red, Dingač, grown on near-vertical vineyards above the Adriatic near the walled town of Ston.

activities.title: Watch the sunset from Zadar's Sea Organ
activities.description: Waves push air through pipes under the pavement, producing tones that change with the sea — Alfred Hitchcock once called Zadar's sunset the most beautiful in the world.

activities.title: Sea kayak under Dubrovnik's walls
activities.description: Paddling the water directly below the fortifications gives a different scale to the walls than walking on top of them does.

activities.title: Eat fresh seafood at a konoba
activities.description: Small family-run taverns serving the day's catch simply grilled, alongside black risotto and Dalmatian-style peka cooked under an iron bell.

activities.title: Hike or bike Mljet National Park
activities.description: An island with two saltwater lakes at its centre, one holding a tiny twelfth-century monastery on an islet — quiet even by Croatian island standards.

activities.title: Explore Pula's Roman amphitheatre
activities.description: One of the best-preserved Roman arenas anywhere, still used for concerts and film screenings nearly two thousand years after it was built.

activities.title: Take the cable car up Dubrovnik's Srđ hill
activities.description: A few minutes up for a full panorama of the Old Town, the walls and the islands offshore — best timed for sunset.

activities.title: Sail your own route down the coast
activities.description: A well-developed charter industry makes it realistic to skipper a boat yourself between islands, or hire a skipper if you'd rather not.

activities.title: Visit the Museum of Broken Relationships in Zagreb
activities.description: An unusual, genuinely moving collection of objects donated by strangers, each with a short story about a relationship that ended.

activities.title: Spend a day in Zagreb's Upper Town
activities.description: Croatia's inland capital, often skipped for the coast, with a walkable historic centre, a funicular, and a food and market culture worth the detour.

snapshot.visa: Visa-free 90 days (Schengen) for US/UK/EU

countries.name: Rwanda
countries.blurb: Steep hills terraced with tea and banana, a rebuilt capital that runs cleaner than most in Africa, and the misted bamboo forests where the last mountain gorillas hold on.
countries.uniqueness: Rwanda is nicknamed the land of a thousand hills for a reason — almost no ground in the country is flat, which shapes everything from its farming terraces to its permit-only, small-group approach to gorilla trekking. It's also one of the few countries where mountain gorilla numbers have been rising rather than falling, the direct result of tourism revenue funding the conservation that protects them.

seasons.label: Long dry season
seasons.note: The most reliable trekking conditions of the year — firm trails, lower malaria risk, and the busiest, most expensive permit season.

seasons.label: Short dry season
seasons.note: A second solid trekking window with generally comfortable weather, quieter than the June–September peak.

seasons.label: Long rains
seasons.note: The heaviest rain of the year and the muddiest trekking conditions, but permits are easier to get and prices sometimes drop.

seasons.label: Short rains
seasons.note: Lighter, more intermittent rain than the long wet season — a reasonable trade-off between crowds, cost and conditions.

activities.title: Trek mountain gorillas in Volcanoes National Park
activities.description: Permits are limited and expensive by design, capping each habituated family group at eight visitors a day for one hour with the gorillas once found.

activities.title: Trek golden monkeys
activities.description: A less-booked, less-expensive permit than gorilla trekking, in the same bamboo forest, for an endangered species found almost nowhere else.

activities.title: Hike a Volcanoes National Park peak
activities.description: Mount Bisoke's crater lake and Mount Karisimbi's multi-day summit push are open to trekkers with a separate permit from the gorilla treks.

activities.title: Track chimpanzees in Nyungwe Forest
activities.description: One of Africa's oldest rainforests, home to habituated chimp communities and a canopy walkway suspended sixty metres up.

activities.title: Walk the Nyungwe canopy walkway
activities.description: A swaying suspension bridge through the forest canopy, one of few of its kind in Africa, with views over an unbroken rainforest canopy.

activities.title: Visit the Kigali Genocide Memorial
activities.description: A sober, essential stop in the capital — the resting place of more than 250,000 victims of the 1994 genocide, with exhibits explaining how it happened and what followed.

activities.title: Spend a morning at Kigali's markets
activities.description: Kimironko Market is the city's biggest, selling produce, fabric and everyday goods in a covered maze of stalls that rewards slow browsing.

activities.title: Safari in Akagera National Park
activities.description: Rwanda's own Big Five park in the east, rebuilt from near-collapse after the genocide through a well-regarded conservation partnership — now home to lion and rhino again.

activities.title: Boat safari on Lake Ihema
activities.description: Akagera's largest lake, with hippos and crocodiles visible from the water and a different pace than a game drive.

activities.title: Relax at Lake Kivu
activities.description: One of Africa's great lakes, calm enough to swim in and dotted with small towns like Gisenyi and Kibuye that make an easy add-on after trekking.

activities.title: Visit a Rwandan tea plantation
activities.description: The volcanic soil and altitude around Nyungwe and the northern hills produce tea grown on impossibly steep, neatly terraced slopes.

activities.title: Learn traditional dance and drumming
activities.description: Intore dance troupes perform a warrior dance developed for the royal court, now kept alive through cultural centres and community visits.

activities.title: Visit the King's Palace Museum in Nyanza
activities.description: A reconstruction of the traditional royal residence, including the long-horned Inyambo cattle once kept specifically for the king.

activities.title: Walk through a Kigali cooperative craft workshop
activities.description: Agaseke basket weaving and other crafts are often organized through women's cooperatives, giving a direct look at a skill passed down through generations.

activities.title: Bird-watch in Nyungwe Forest
activities.description: Over 300 species recorded, including the Albertine Rift endemics that draw birders from well outside the primate-trekking crowd.

activities.title: Eat at a Kigali brochette spot
activities.description: Grilled skewers, usually goat or beef, sold at informal grills and proper restaurants alike — a good introduction to everyday Rwandan food alongside plantain and beans.

activities.title: Cycle the Congo Nile Trail
activities.description: A multi-day route tracing Lake Kivu's shoreline through fishing villages and terraced hills, doable by bike or on foot in shorter sections.

activities.title: Take a coffee tour near Lake Kivu
activities.description: Rwandan coffee has built a strong specialty reputation since the early 2000s — cooperative farms around the lake walk visitors from cherry to cup.

activities.title: Visit the Ellen DeGeneres Campus of the Dian Fossey Gorilla Fund
activities.description: A research and education centre near Volcanoes National Park continuing the work of the primatologist who first drew the world's attention to the mountain gorillas.

activities.title: Watch the sunrise over the Virunga volcano chain
activities.description: Five volcanic peaks straddling Rwanda, Uganda and the DRC, visible from Volcanoes National Park's lodges at dawn before cloud typically builds in.

snapshot.visa: Visa on arrival or e-visa, about $50 (free for AU/Commonwealth/Francophonie citizens)

faq.q: Is Rwanda safe to visit?
faq.a: Yes — Rwanda is consistently ranked among the safest countries in Africa for tourists, with low street crime and a strong, visible police presence in Kigali and around the parks. Standard travel precautions still apply, especially around border areas with the DRC, which most itineraries don't go near.

faq.q: How much does gorilla trekking cost?
faq.a: A gorilla trekking permit is $1,500 per person as of 2026, booked directly through the Rwanda Development Board or a tour operator. That fee funds the conservation work that's brought mountain gorilla numbers back from the edge, and it's non-negotiable — every visitor pays the same price.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Rwanda?
faq.a: Most people manage a good trip in 5-7 days: two for gorilla or golden monkey trekking around Volcanoes National Park, one or two for Nyungwe's chimps and canopy walk, and a day or two around Kigali and Lake Kivu.

faq.q: Do I need a visa for Rwanda?
faq.a: Most nationalities can get a visa on arrival or apply for an e-visa in advance, generally around $50. Citizens of African Union, Commonwealth, and La Francophonie member countries can often get a free 30-day visa on arrival. Check the exact rules for your passport before you fly.

faq.q: What's the best time to see the gorillas?
faq.a: June through September is the long dry season and the most reliable trekking window — firm trails and the lowest malaria risk. December through February is a shorter dry season that's nearly as good and usually quieter.

faq.q: Is Rwanda expensive?
faq.a: Gorilla permits push the average trip cost up regardless of everything else, so Rwanda reads as a $$$ destination even though food, local transport, and city accommodation are inexpensive by comparison. Budget travelers who skip trekking can visit very cheaply.

countries.name: Tanzania
countries.blurb: The Serengeti's endless plains, Kilimanjaro's snowcap on the equator, and the white-sand calm of Zanzibar — three completely different trips inside one country.
countries.uniqueness: Tanzania holds the largest share of the Serengeti-Mara ecosystem, so the Great Migration spends most of the year on its side of the border, not Kenya's. It's also one of the few countries where you can plausibly combine a snow-capped mountain summit, a Big Five safari, and a tropical island in a single two-week trip.

snapshot.visa: e-Visa or visa on arrival, roughly $50-100 depending on nationality

seasons.label: Long dry season
seasons.note: The classic safari window — thinning vegetation and scarce water concentrate wildlife, and the migration's river crossings peak July–September.

seasons.label: Short dry season
seasons.note: Warm and mostly dry, with the migration's calving season on the southern Serengeti plains in January and February.

seasons.label: Long rains
seasons.note: The wettest, quietest stretch — some camps close, but rates drop sharply and the light for photography is excellent.

seasons.label: Zanzibar high season
seasons.note: The coast follows its own rhythm; these windows avoid the heaviest rain and give the calmest, clearest water.

activities.title: Watch the migration cross the Mara River
activities.description: Wildebeest and zebra funnel across crocodile-filled water on the Tanzanian side of the same ecosystem Kenya's Mara belongs to.

activities.title: Go on safari in the Serengeti
activities.description: Endless short-grass plains that give the park its Maasai name — lion, cheetah and leopard sightings here are as reliable as anywhere in Africa.

activities.title: Descend into the Ngorongoro Crater
activities.description: A collapsed volcanic caldera holding one of the densest concentrations of wildlife on the continent, including some of Tanzania's last black rhino.

activities.title: Watch flamingos on Lake Manyara
activities.description: A shallow soda lake beneath the Rift Valley escarpment, known for tree-climbing lions and huge flocks of flamingo depending on algae levels.

activities.title: Climb Mount Kilimanjaro
activities.description: Africa's highest peak and the world's tallest freestanding mountain, climbable without technical gear on routes like Machame or Marangu over five to nine days.

activities.title: Relax on Zanzibar's beaches
activities.description: Powder-white sand and turquoise water on the east coast at Paje and Jambiani, with kitesurfing schools and a much slower pace than the mainland.

activities.title: Wander Stone Town
activities.description: Zanzibar's UNESCO-listed old quarter — carved wooden doors, spice markets and Swahili-Arab architecture layered by centuries of Indian Ocean trade.

activities.title: Take a Zanzibar spice tour
activities.description: Clove, cardamom, vanilla and pepper plantations on an island once known as the Spice Island, with tastings straight off the plant.

activities.title: Snorkel or dive off Mnemba Atoll
activities.description: A protected marine reserve off Zanzibar's north coast with some of the clearest water and richest reef life in the region.

activities.title: Track chimpanzees in Mahale Mountains
activities.description: A remote, boat-access-only park on Lake Tanganyika's shore, holding one of the largest wild chimpanzee populations left in Africa.

activities.title: Walk with a Maasai guide
activities.description: Community-run cultural visits near Ngorongoro and the Serengeti offer a look at a pastoralist life that continues alongside the safari industry.

activities.title: Safari the southern circuit
activities.description: Ruaha and Selous (now Nyerere) see a fraction of the northern parks' traffic, with big elephant herds and wild dog sightings for those who've done the Serengeti before.

activities.title: Go on a walking safari
activities.description: A handful of southern camps offer armed-guide walking safaris — slower and more attentive to tracks and smaller life than a vehicle allows.

activities.title: Watch the sunset over the Serengeti plains
activities.description: No fixed spot — just wherever the game drive is when the light turns gold, which is often when predators start moving again.

activities.title: Visit Olduvai Gorge
activities.description: One of the most important paleoanthropological sites on earth, where fossil finds pushed back the known timeline of human origins by millions of years.

activities.title: Sail a traditional dhow at sunset
activities.description: Wooden sailboats that have worked the Zanzibar channel for centuries, now also run as sunset cruises out of Stone Town harbour.

activities.title: Eat street food on Forodhani Gardens
activities.description: Stone Town's waterfront night market — Zanzibar pizza, grilled octopus and sugarcane juice sold from stalls as the sun goes down.

activities.title: Hike in the Usambara Mountains
activities.description: A cooler, greener corner of northern Tanzania with terraced farms and forest trails, rarely visited despite being an easy detour from the safari circuit.

activities.title: Visit a coffee farm near Kilimanjaro
activities.description: The volcanic soil on Kilimanjaro's lower slopes has grown arabica coffee for over a century — small farms around Moshi run tours and tastings.

activities.title: Kayak the mangroves of Zanzibar's Chwaka Bay
activities.description: A quiet paddle through tidal mangrove channels, well off the main resort strip, with local fishermen still working the same waters.

activities.title: Balloon over the Serengeti at dawn
activities.description: A sunrise float over the plains ending in a bush breakfast — one of the more expensive mornings on the circuit, and rarely regretted.

countries.name: South Africa
countries.blurb: Big Five safari, Cape wine country and a coastline where two oceans meet — a country that packs an entire continent's range of landscape into one trip.
countries.uniqueness: South Africa has three capital cities, splitting legislative, judicial and administrative power between Cape Town, Bloemfontein and Pretoria — a compromise from its founding. It's also one of the only places on earth where you can safari for Big Five game and surf or whale-watch on a world-class coastline within a single day's drive.

snapshot.visa: Visa-free up to 90 days for US/UK/most EU

seasons.label: Kruger dry season
seasons.note: Thinning bush and scarce water concentrate wildlife around rivers and pans — the most reliable window for game viewing.

seasons.label: Cape Town summer
seasons.note: Warm, dry and sunny on the Cape — peak season for beaches, hiking and the winelands, opposite Kruger's wet season.

seasons.label: Whale season
seasons.note: Southern right whales calve close to shore along the Western Cape, with Hermanus among the best land-based whale-watching spots anywhere.

seasons.label: Shoulder months
seasons.note: A reasonable compromise between Kruger's dry season and Cape Town's summer, with fewer crowds than either peak.

activities.title: Go on safari in Kruger National Park
activities.description: One of Africa's largest and most accessible parks, with a road network good enough to self-drive as well as guided options across all budgets.

activities.title: Track the Big Five in a private reserve
activities.description: Sabi Sands and other reserves bordering Kruger allow off-road tracking and night drives that the national park itself doesn't permit.

activities.title: Ride the cable car up Table Mountain
activities.description: A rotating cable car to a flat-topped summit with views over Cape Town, the Atlantic and the peninsula stretching south.

activities.title: Drive the Cape Peninsula to Cape Point
activities.description: A coastal road past Chapman's Peak, penguin colonies at Boulders Beach and the windswept cliffs where two oceans are said to meet.

activities.title: Taste wine in Stellenbosch and Franschhoek
activities.description: Cape Dutch estates set against mountain backdrops, producing some of the southern hemisphere's best Cabernet, Chenin Blanc and Cap Classique.

activities.title: Watch southern right whales from Hermanus
activities.description: Whales come close enough to shore here that a whale-crier walks the town blowing a kelp horn to announce sightings.

activities.title: Surf or swim at Muizenberg
activities.description: Cape Town's classic beginner surf beach, backed by candy-coloured Victorian bathing huts and a laid-back village feel.

activities.title: Walk through District Six and the Bo-Kaap
activities.description: A former forced-removal site turned museum, and a hillside neighbourhood of brightly painted houses with deep Cape Malay roots — two sides of Cape Town's layered history.

activities.title: Visit Robben Island
activities.description: The prison island where Nelson Mandela spent eighteen of his twenty-seven years in custody, now a museum run partly by former political prisoners as guides.

activities.title: Hike the Drakensberg escarpment
activities.description: South Africa's highest mountain range, with trails ranging from a day hike to multi-day treks past waterfalls and San rock art.

activities.title: Shark cage dive in Gansbaai
activities.description: One of the world's most reliable great white shark spots, though sightings have become less predictable in recent years as populations shift — check current operator reports.

activities.title: Drive the Garden Route
activities.description: A coastal road between Cape Town and Port Elizabeth stringing together forests, lagoons, bungee jumps and small beach towns over about a week.

activities.title: Bungee jump at Bloukrans Bridge
activities.description: One of the highest commercial bungee jumps on earth, 216 metres above the Bloukrans River gorge on the Garden Route.

activities.title: Eat a proper braai
activities.description: South African barbecue culture runs deeper than the food itself — it's a social institution, and most guesthouses and lodges will happily host one.

activities.title: Visit the Apartheid Museum in Johannesburg
activities.description: An unflinching, well-built museum covering the rise and fall of apartheid, widely regarded as essential context before or after a safari trip.

activities.title: Track rhino in Hluhluwe-iMfolozi
activities.description: The oldest proclaimed nature reserve in Africa, and the place credited with saving the southern white rhino from near-extinction last century.

activities.title: Relax on the beaches of Durban
activities.description: A warmer, more tropical coastline than the Cape, with a strong Indian Ocean surf culture and some of the country's best curry houses.

activities.title: Explore the Cango Caves
activities.description: A network of dramatic limestone caverns near Oudtshoorn on the Garden Route, with chambers large enough to hold concerts.

activities.title: Visit an ostrich farm in the Karoo
activities.description: Oudtshoorn built its economy on ostrich feathers a century ago and still farms them today — tours cover everything from eggs to an ostrich-back ride.

activities.title: Watch the sunset from Signal Hill
activities.description: A short drive above Cape Town for a full panorama over the city bowl, Table Mountain and the Atlantic coast.

countries.name: Switzerland
countries.blurb: Sawtooth peaks, glacial lakes and trains that run so precisely you could set a watch by them — a small country built almost entirely on mountains.
countries.uniqueness: Switzerland isn't in the EU but sits inside the Schengen area, and its rail network is often called the best in the world — trains, boats and cable cars are timed to connect within minutes of each other, even in remote valleys. Four national languages (German, French, Italian, Romansh) shift by region, sometimes within the same canton.

snapshot.visa: Visa-free 90 days (Schengen) for US/UK/EU

seasons.label: Winter
seasons.note: Peak ski season in resorts like Zermatt, Verbier and St. Moritz, with Christmas markets in the lowland cities.

seasons.label: Spring
seasons.note: Snow retreats from lower trails, waterfalls run high on snowmelt, and crowds and prices are both lower than summer.

seasons.label: Summer
seasons.note: The classic hiking season with full alpine trail access — also the busiest and most expensive months in the mountain resorts.

seasons.label: Autumn
seasons.note: Clear air, larch trees turning gold, and noticeably thinner crowds — often rated the best all-round hiking window.

activities.title: Ride the Glacier Express
activities.description: An eight-hour panoramic train between Zermatt and St. Moritz crossing 291 bridges and 91 tunnels through the heart of the Alps.

activities.title: Hike beneath the Matterhorn
activities.description: Zermatt's car-free village sits directly under one of the most recognisable peaks on earth, with trail networks for every fitness level radiating out from town.

activities.title: Take the cog railway up the Jungfraujoch
activities.description: Europe's highest railway station, over 3,400 metres up, with an ice palace carved into the glacier and views across the Aletsch, the Alps' longest glacier.

activities.title: Cruise Lake Geneva
activities.description: Belle Époque paddle steamers connect lakeside towns like Montreux and Lausanne, backed by vineyard terraces climbing straight from the shore.

activities.title: Explore Lucerne's old town
activities.description: A medieval covered wooden bridge, a lakefront promenade and a well-preserved old town make Lucerne one of the most photogenic stops on any itinerary.

activities.title: Ski or snowboard in Verbier or St. Moritz
activities.description: Two of the Alps' most storied resorts, with terrain ranging from groomed pistes to genuine off-piste and heli-skiing.

activities.title: Walk the vineyard terraces of Lavaux
activities.description: A UNESCO World Heritage stretch of steep vineyards above Lake Geneva, walkable on marked paths between small wine villages.

activities.title: Visit the Rhine Falls
activities.description: The largest waterfall in Europe by volume, near Schaffhausen, with viewing platforms and boat trips that get close to the spray.

activities.title: Eat fondue in a mountain hut
activities.description: Melted cheese, bread and a glass of Fendant is the classic alpine meal — best eaten after a day on the trails, not before.

activities.title: Paraglide over the Lauterbrunnen valley
activities.description: A valley of 72 waterfalls dropping from sheer cliffs, seen from above on a tandem paraglide launched from Mürren or Wengen.

activities.title: Ride a cable car to the Schilthorn
activities.description: A revolving restaurant at the summit and a 360-degree view across the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau, reached without any hiking required.

activities.title: Spend a day in Zurich
activities.description: Switzerland's largest city mixes old-town cobblestones with a genuinely good contemporary art and design scene, plus swimming spots right in the lake.

activities.title: Walk to a waterfall in the Bernese Oberland
activities.description: Trümmelbach Falls run inside the mountain itself — glacial meltwater from the Eiger and Jungfrau carved a series of underground chutes now open to walk through.

activities.title: Visit a chocolate or cheese workshop
activities.description: Gruyères pairs its namesake cheese dairy with a chocolate factory nearby — both open for tours and tastings in the same afternoon.

activities.title: Hike the Five Lakes Trail near Zermatt
activities.description: A route linking five small alpine lakes, several of which reflect the Matterhorn on a still day — one of the most photographed hikes in the country.

activities.title: Explore Bern's old town
activities.description: Switzerland's capital is a UNESCO World Heritage medieval centre with arcaded streets, a bear park, and the Aare river locals swim down in summer.

activities.title: Ride the Bernina Express
activities.description: A UNESCO-listed rail route crossing from Switzerland into Italy over the Bernina Pass, including an open-air panoramic carriage in summer.

activities.title: Soak in a thermal spa after a day on the trails
activities.description: Leukerbad and other alpine towns have thermal baths fed by natural hot springs, a genuinely restorative end to a hiking day.

activities.title: Visit CERN near Geneva
activities.description: The world's largest particle physics laboratory offers free public tours and exhibits explaining the Large Hadron Collider in accessible terms.

activities.title: Watch the sunrise from a mountain hut
activities.description: Overnighting in a staffed alpine hut and catching first light on the surrounding peaks is a low-key highlight for anyone doing a multi-day hike.

countries.name: India
countries.blurb: Mughal marble, Himalayan foothills, backwater canals and street food that rewards the adventurous — a country too vast and varied to see in one trip, and most people know it.
countries.uniqueness: India is less one destination than a continent's worth of them under one flag — a desert state, a tropical coast, and the world's highest mountain range are all within its borders, each with its own language, cuisine and rhythm. Most first-time visitors pick one region rather than attempting the whole country at once, and that's the right instinct.

snapshot.visa: e-Visa required for most nationalities, apply online in advance
snapshot.languages: Hindi, English, and 20+ official regional languages

seasons.label: Winter
seasons.note: India's peak season for most regions — cool, dry and comfortable for sightseeing in Rajasthan, Delhi and the south.

seasons.label: Summer
seasons.note: Punishingly hot across most of the plains, though hill stations like Shimla and the Himalayan foothills offer relief.

seasons.label: Monsoon
seasons.note: Heavy rain across most of the country — Kerala's backwaters and lush landscapes are at their most dramatic, but travel elsewhere gets harder.

seasons.label: Post-monsoon
seasons.note: Green landscapes, clearing skies, and one of the best windows to combine sightseeing with more comfortable temperatures.

activities.title: See the Taj Mahal at sunrise
activities.description: The marble mausoleum changes colour through the day — dawn brings the softest light and the thinnest crowds before tour buses arrive from Delhi.

activities.title: Explore Rajasthan's forts and palaces
activities.description: Jaipur's Amber Fort, Jodhpur's Mehrangarh and Udaipur's lake palaces trace centuries of Rajput and Mughal history across the desert state.

activities.title: Cruise Kerala's backwaters
activities.description: A network of canals, lagoons and lakes behind the Malabar coast, traditionally toured on a converted rice barge called a houseboat.
activities.when: Nov–Feb, or monsoon for lushest scenery

activities.title: Watch the sunrise over Varanasi's ghats
activities.description: One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities on earth, where cremation rites, morning prayer and daily bathing all happen along the same riverbank.

activities.title: Trek in the Himalayan foothills
activities.description: Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand offer accessible multi-day treks through pine forest and alpine meadows without needing high-altitude experience.

activities.title: Eat street food in Old Delhi
activities.description: Chandni Chowk's lanes have fed the city for centuries — parathas, chaat and kebabs from stalls that have often run in the same family for generations.

activities.title: Ride a houseboat in Srinagar
activities.description: Kashmir's Dal Lake has hosted floating cedar-wood houseboats since the colonial era, with shikara boats still ferrying goods and flowers each morning.

activities.title: Visit Amritsar's Golden Temple
activities.description: Sikhism's holiest site, plated in real gold and open to visitors of any faith, including the langar hall serving free meals to tens of thousands daily.

activities.title: Go on a tiger safari
activities.description: Ranthambore, Bandhavgarh and Kanha national parks give some of the best realistic odds anywhere of seeing a wild Bengal tiger.

activities.title: Take a cooking class in Kerala or Rajasthan
activities.description: Regional Indian cooking varies dramatically by state — a hands-on class is often the fastest way to actually understand the difference.

activities.title: Explore Hampi's ruins
activities.description: The remains of a fourteenth-century Vijayanagara capital scattered across a surreal boulder landscape in Karnataka — vast, half-forgotten, and rarely crowded.

activities.title: Relax on Goa's beaches
activities.description: Former Portuguese colony with a beach culture split between backpacker shacks in the north and quieter resorts in the south.

activities.title: Watch the Ganga Aarti ceremony
activities.description: An evening fire ritual performed on the riverbank at Varanasi and Rishikesh — chanting, bells and floating oil lamps set adrift on the water.

activities.title: Ride the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway
activities.description: A UNESCO-listed narrow-gauge steam railway climbing into the tea-growing hills of West Bengal, with views toward Kangchenjunga on a clear day.

activities.title: Tour a Darjeeling or Assam tea estate
activities.description: India's two most famous tea-growing regions offer plantation walks and tastings that explain why the leaves from each taste so different.

activities.title: Visit Mumbai's Dhobi Ghat and markets
activities.description: An open-air laundry employing thousands, alongside Crawford Market and Colaba's street stalls — a fast, dense introduction to India's largest city.

activities.title: See the sun temple at Konark
activities.description: A thirteenth-century temple built as a giant stone chariot with carved wheels, dedicated to the sun god and among India's finest architectural achievements.

activities.title: Do a yoga retreat in Rishikesh
activities.description: The self-declared yoga capital of the world, on the Ganges where it first leaves the Himalayan foothills — ashrams here range from serious to casual.

activities.title: Explore the caves of Ajanta and Ellora
activities.description: Rock-cut Buddhist, Hindu and Jain temples carved directly into cliff faces over a thousand years, among the most significant ancient sites in Asia.

activities.title: Watch the Wagah border ceremony
activities.description: A theatrical daily flag-lowering ritual at the India-Pakistan border near Amritsar, performed with high kicks and crowds cheering from both sides.

countries.name: Sri Lanka
countries.blurb: Tea hills, elephant-filled national parks and a coastline split by two monsoons — a small island where you can go from beach to rainforest to ancient ruins in the space of a day's drive.
countries.uniqueness: Sri Lanka's two coasts are governed by opposite monsoons, so there's almost always a dry, sunny side of the island somewhere — the trick is knowing which one, and when. Despite its size, it holds eight UNESCO World Heritage Sites, more per square kilometre than almost anywhere else in Asia.

snapshot.visa: ETA required for most nationalities, now free for 40 countries including US/UK as of May 2026
snapshot.languages: Sinhala, Tamil; English widely spoken in tourism

seasons.label: Southwest dry season
seasons.note: The best window for the south and west coasts and the hill country — sunny, dry, and the busiest tourist season.

seasons.label: Northeast dry season
seasons.note: While the southwest gets its monsoon rains, the east coast around Arugam Bay and Trincomalee is dry, sunny and much quieter.

seasons.label: Shoulder months
seasons.note: Transitional weather on both coasts, with lower prices and thinner crowds than either peak season.

seasons.label: Hill country
seasons.note: Nuwara Eliya and the tea hills stay noticeably cooler than the coast at any time of year, with their own light, unpredictable rain pattern.

activities.title: Climb Sigiriya Rock Fortress
activities.description: A fifth-century royal citadel built atop a 200-metre volcanic column, with frescoes, water gardens and a stairway through a giant lion's paws.

activities.title: Go on safari in Yala National Park
activities.description: One of the highest leopard densities anywhere in the world, alongside elephant, sloth bear and crocodile in the island's most-visited park.

activities.title: Ride the train from Kandy to Ella
activities.description: Widely called one of the most beautiful train journeys in the world, winding through tea plantations, waterfalls and misty hill country.

activities.title: Watch elephants at Udawalawe or Minneriya
activities.description: Minneriya's dry-season elephant gathering can draw hundreds of animals to a single reservoir — one of Asia's most dramatic wildlife spectacles.

activities.title: Explore the ancient city of Polonnawa
activities.description: A well-preserved medieval capital with carved Buddha statues, royal ruins and temple complexes, easily explored by bicycle in a morning.

activities.title: Surf at Arugam Bay
activities.description: The island's best-known surf town on the east coast, with a long right-hand point break that draws surfers from across Asia.

activities.title: Walk the ramparts of Galle Fort
activities.description: A Dutch colonial fort on the southwest coast, its walls enclosing a UNESCO-listed old town of boutique shops, cafes and colonial architecture.

activities.title: Tour a tea estate in Nuwara Eliya
activities.description: Ceylon tea built the colonial hill-station economy — plantation tours here explain the process from leaf to cup against genuinely stunning scenery.

activities.title: Whale watch from Mirissa
activities.description: One of the few places in the world to reliably spot blue whales, the largest animal on earth, alongside sperm whales and dolphins.

activities.title: Climb Adam's Peak overnight
activities.description: A pilgrimage trail climbed in darkness so hikers reach the summit shrine by sunrise, sacred to four different religions on the island.

activities.title: Relax on the beaches of Mirissa or Unawatuna
activities.description: Palm-lined south-coast beaches with a laid-back, backpacker-friendly scene and some of the island's best sunset views.

activities.title: Visit the Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
activities.description: Kandy's most important Buddhist site, said to house one of Buddha's teeth, at the centre of the city's daily religious life and its major annual festival.

activities.title: Hike through Horton Plains to World's End
activities.description: A highland plateau trail ending at a sheer cliff dropping nearly 900 metres — best started at dawn before cloud rolls in.

activities.title: Eat a proper rice and curry spread
activities.description: The island's everyday meal — several small curries, sambols and rice served together, varying meaningfully from Tamil to Sinhala to coastal kitchens.

activities.title: Snorkel the reefs at Pigeon Island
activities.description: A marine national park off Trincomalee with shallow reefs, reef sharks and turtles easily accessible without a boat dive certification.

activities.title: Explore the cave temples of Dambulla
activities.description: Five caves carved into a granite outcrop, painted with Buddhist murals and housing dozens of Buddha statues, some dating back over two thousand years.

activities.title: Go white-water rafting near Kitulgala
activities.description: The island's main whitewater run, on the river where parts of The Bridge on the River Kwai were filmed, with rapids suited to beginners.

activities.title: Visit a spice garden near Matale
activities.description: Small family-run gardens growing cinnamon, cardamom, pepper and vanilla, with tours explaining the island's centuries-old spice trade.

activities.title: Watch stilt fishermen at Weligama
activities.description: A dwindling but still-practiced fishing technique unique to Sri Lanka's south coast, fishermen perched on poles planted just offshore.

activities.title: Wander the botanical gardens at Peradeniya
activities.description: One of the finest tropical botanical gardens in Asia, near Kandy, with an avenue of royal palms and orchid houses spanning 147 acres.

countries.name: Jordan
countries.blurb: A rose-red city carved into sandstone cliffs, a desert that looks like Mars, and the lowest, saltiest water on earth — small, safe, and stacked with landscape.
countries.uniqueness: Jordan is one of the more stable and tourist-friendly countries in the Middle East, and it packs an outsized range of landscape into a small footprint — you can stand in Wadi Rum's Mars-red desert in the morning and float in the Dead Sea, the lowest point on earth's land surface, by afternoon. Petra alone was voted one of the New Seven Wonders of the World and still isn't fully excavated.

snapshot.visa: Visa on arrival, ~$56 — waived with a Jordan Pass if staying 3+ nights
snapshot.languages: Arabic; English widely spoken in tourism

seasons.label: Spring
seasons.note: Widely considered Petra and Wadi Rum's best season — mild temperatures, clear light, and occasional desert wildflowers.

seasons.label: Summer
seasons.note: Intense heat, often exceeding 35°C at Petra and higher in the Dead Sea valley — manageable with an early start, and noticeably quieter.

seasons.label: Autumn
seasons.note: A second sweet spot with fewer crowds than spring and similarly comfortable temperatures.

seasons.label: Winter
seasons.note: Cold at Petra's elevation, sometimes near freezing at night, with occasional snow — the quietest and cheapest season by far.

activities.title: Walk the Siq into Petra
activities.description: A narrow sandstone canyon opening suddenly onto the Treasury facade — still one of the great reveal moments in travel, best done at first light.

activities.title: See Petra by candlelight
activities.description: Three evenings a week the Siq is lined with candles leading to a Bedouin music performance at the Treasury after dark.
activities.when: Mon, Wed, Thu evenings, check schedule

activities.title: Camp overnight in Wadi Rum
activities.description: A desert of red sand and towering sandstone monoliths, still home to Bedouin communities running Mars-like camps under some of the clearest night skies in the region.

activities.title: Float in the Dead Sea
activities.description: Water so dense with salt and minerals that sinking is genuinely impossible — most resorts along the shore offer mineral mud alongside the float itself.

activities.title: Hike Petra's back trails to the Monastery
activities.description: Nearly 900 steps lead up to Ad-Deir, a monument larger than the Treasury and far less crowded, especially in the late afternoon.

activities.title: Drive or 4x4 through Wadi Rum's desert
activities.description: Bedouin-guided jeep tours reach rock bridges, ancient inscriptions and canyons that aren't walkable from the main camps.

activities.title: Explore the Roman ruins at Jerash
activities.description: One of the best-preserved Roman provincial cities anywhere, with a colonnaded main street, amphitheatres and temples still largely intact.

activities.title: Eat mansaf, Jordan's national dish
activities.description: Lamb cooked in fermented dried yogurt sauce over rice, traditionally eaten by hand and shared from a communal platter at celebrations.

activities.title: Snorkel or dive the Red Sea at Aqaba
activities.description: Jordan's only coastline, with coral reefs, a sunken tank and shipwrecks accessible close to shore, and warmer water than the Mediterranean side of the region.

activities.title: Watch the sunset from Petra's High Place of Sacrifice
activities.description: A steep climb above the Treasury to a Nabataean ritual site with panoramic views over the whole ancient city.

activities.title: Visit Mount Nebo
activities.description: The site where Moses is said to have viewed the Promised Land before his death, with views across the Jordan Valley to Jerusalem on a clear day.

activities.title: Wander the souks of downtown Amman
activities.description: Gold, spice and fabric markets in the older, lower part of the capital, alongside the Roman theatre carved into a hillside in the city centre.

activities.title: Ride a camel or horse into Wadi Rum
activities.description: The traditional way to enter the desert, still offered alongside jeep tours, moving slowly enough to actually take in the scale of the landscape.

activities.title: Soak in the hot springs at Ma'in
activities.description: Waterfalls of naturally heated mineral water cascading into pools near the Dead Sea, a mineral-rich contrast to the sea's still, salty float.

activities.title: Visit the ancient mosaics of Madaba
activities.description: Known as the City of Mosaics, its Byzantine-era church floor holds the oldest surviving map of the Holy Land, made from two million tiny pieces.

activities.title: Star-gaze from a Wadi Rum desert camp
activities.description: Minimal light pollution and clear desert air make this one of the best accessible stargazing spots in the Middle East.

activities.title: Explore the crusader castle at Kerak
activities.description: A hilltop fortress built by crusaders in the twelfth century, later expanded by Islamic forces, with tunnels and halls still open to explore.

activities.title: Try Bedouin-style zarb cooking
activities.description: Meat and vegetables slow-cooked underground over hot coals, then unearthed in a small ceremony — a specialty of desert camps in Wadi Rum.

activities.title: Hike the Jordan Trail
activities.description: A 675km long-distance route running the length of the country, from Um Qais to Aqaba — most visitors walk a section rather than the whole thing.

activities.title: Rock scramble in the Jebel Rum massif
activities.description: Scrambling routes up Wadi Rum's sandstone peaks for those who want more than a jeep tour, generally done with a local Bedouin guide.
